title: Trust rotation can commit on disk while reporting failure and rolling memory back
description: CORRECTNESS: TrustStore.rotate_key mutates the in-memory snapshot, calls TrustStorePersistence.save, and on any exception restores the old in-memory entry/revision. But TrustStorePersistence._write_json_locked performs os.replace before chmod and directory fsync. If either post-replace operation raises, save reports failure even though trust_store.json already contains the rotated key and advanced revision. rotate_key then restores old memory, so runtime and durable trust disagree; restart accepts a rotation the caller was told failed, and subsequent saves fail stale-revision CAS. Treat the post-replace state as an indeterminate/terminal persistence transition or redesign commit/reconciliation so an exception cannot produce a durable new snapshot with old live memory. Add injected chmod/directory-fsync failure tests around public rotation.
